comparisons.peer_summary: Net income for Global Markets increased $944 million to $5.6 billion, with net DVA losses decreasing to $113 million from $236 million in 2023; excluding net DVA, net income rose $851 million to $5.7 billion.
comparisons.comparison: C's All Other-Managed Basis and BAC's Global Markets segment both reported increased net income in 2024 primarily driven by higher revenues. C reported net income of $1.5 billion, up from a loss, with revenues increasing 32% due to Investment Banking and Corporate Lending. BAC reported Global Markets net income of $5.6 billion, up $944 million, driven by higher revenue (though partially offset by expense increases). Both segments reflect strong performance in capital markets-related activities (C: Investment Banking/Corporate Lending; BAC: Global Markets/Sales & Trading implied by context).

sentences.text: Net income was $1.5 billion, compared to a net loss of $35 million in the prior year, driven by higher revenues, lower expenses and a higher benefit from cost of credit.

Revenues increased 32% (including losses on loan hedges), reflecting higher Investment Banking and Corporate Lending revenues, along with a lower loss on loan hedges ($180 million versus $443 million in the prior year).
Net income for Global Markets increased $944 million to $5.6 billion.
These increases were primarily driven by higher revenue, partially offset by higher noninterest expense.

peer_results.rationale: GS candidates focus on specific loan portfolio details (Private Banking and Lending) or credit card provision drivers (Platform Solutions). GS Private Banking details gross loan balances and average loans, which is a balance sheet composition metric, whereas C's All Other-Managed Basis disclosure is a P&L performance summary. GS Platform Solutions focuses on the increase in provision for credit losses driven by net charge-offs, whereas C reports a provision benefit. The topics (balance sheet composition, specific charge-off drivers) are not substantively comparable to C's broad segment revenue and net income performance.

comparisons.peer_topic: Corporate segment net income and revenue growth
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the Corporate segment reported net income of $10.6 billion and net revenue of $17.4 billion, significant increases from the prior year's $2.8 billion and $8.0 billion respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM report their 'Corporate' segments (C: All Other-Managed Basis, JPM: Corporate) showing significant net income growth driven by revenue increases and credit provision benefits. C reported net income of $1.5 billion compared to a loss in the prior year, driven by 32% revenue growth and a $224 million provision benefit. Similarly, JPM's Corporate segment reported net income of $10.6 billion, up from $2.8 billion in the prior year, with net revenue rising to $17.4 billion from $8.0 billion. Both disclosures highlight a shift from prior year losses or lower income to substantial current year profits fueled by revenue dynamics and credit benefits.
